questions.stem: What are the three main stages of the cell cycle?
questions.explanation: The cell cycle consists of three main stages: interphase (where the cell grows and DNA is replicated), mitosis (nuclear division), and cytokinesis (division of the cytoplasm).

questions.stem: Which phase of the cell cycle takes the longest?
questions.explanation: Interphase is the longest phase of the cell cycle, taking up about 90% of the total time. During interphase, the cell grows, carries out normal functions, and replicates its DNA.

questions.stem: During which sub-phase of interphase is DNA replicated?
questions.explanation: DNA replication occurs during the S phase (synthesis phase) of interphase. After the S phase, each chromosome consists of two identical sister chromatids.

questions.stem: What happens during the G1 phase?

options.text: Chromosomes line up in the middle
The cell grows and carries out normal functions

questions.explanation: During G1 (Gap 1), the cell grows in size, produces proteins, and carries out its normal metabolic functions. It is preparing for DNA replication.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of checkpoints in the cell cycle?

options.text: To remove organelles from the cell
To ensure each stage is completed correctly before the next begins
To increase the number of chromosomes

questions.explanation: Checkpoints are control mechanisms that ensure each stage of the cell cycle is completed correctly before the cell progresses to the next stage, preventing errors such as damaged DNA being passed on.

questions.stem: Uncontrolled cell division can lead to:
questions.explanation: When the cell cycle is not properly regulated and cells divide uncontrollably, this can result in the formation of tumours and cancer.

questions.stem: What happens during the G2 phase?

options.text: The cell checks the replicated DNA and prepares for mitosis

questions.explanation: During G2 (Gap 2), the cell checks the replicated DNA for errors and produces proteins needed for mitosis, such as those that form the spindle fibres.
